reviewer.origin: Claude Agent tool subagent, model sonnet, a fresh context with only this brief and its files, launched 2026-10-26 by session_01Mxpoi6tFT3FgKmBvtGjRtS (the writer's session)

evidence: DRAFT, one sentence: ‘Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent - can people have their minds influenced without the conscious agreement of their adult self?’ It appears once in CONTEXT.txt, as the third paragraph of ‘Protecting Yourself from Hypnotists’, straight after the paragraph that ends on the OECD sentence and before ‘As associated with the Silva Mind Control method:’. THE CHANGE: SOURCE.txt’s replaced words are a four-item list sentence and a separate question; the draft is the same four items in the same order joined to the same question with a spaced hyphen, which is what the_change says. Two small things the_change does not spell out: the question now starts with lower-case ‘can’ (follows from the join) and gains ‘the’ (‘without the conscious agreement of their adult self’ for ‘without conscious agreement of their adult self’) - a grammatical fix that changes no meaning. MEANING against SOURCE.txt: the four kinds of agreement/consent and the question whether a mind can be influenced without the adult self’s conscious agreement are all kept, as in the replaced words (his guide states it as ‘A mind can be influenced without the adult self having clearly chosen the influence’; the article already turns that into the question). No claim, fact, name or number added or dropped; there is no named entity, so C04 is absent. READ IN CONTEXT: it follows an OECD sentence about patterns that steer, deceive, coerce or manipulate people toward choices against their interests, so a question about consent is the natural next thought (not abrupt: ‘conscious mind’ in the paragraph before sets up ‘conscious agreement’); ‘their minds’ and ‘their adult self’ both point to ‘people’ in the same sentence; the list works as a topic frame and the dash as the hand-off to the question, a terse list-then-question move that matches the article’s other list-heavy lines (the long channel list in the first paragraph, the four-verb OECD sentence); the Silva Mind Control line that follows answers the question by implication, as it did in the source. A reader may notice ‘Conscious agreement’ at the start and ‘the conscious agreement’ at the end of one sentence; that repeat is inherited from the source (two sentences there) and the question is about exactly the first of the four, so it does a job. TELLS: I walked T01-T29 and C01-C04 on the draft in this context and find none PRESENT. Closest calls: T12 - four parallel noun phrases (it can be read as two pairs) could look like a tidy taxonomy, but they are his published four (‘Conscious agreement is one thing. Unconscious receptivity is another…’), kept as they were, not claimed to be complete, and not made more balanced by the change, so the operation is not happening here; T21 - the sentence is a list plus a question joined by a dash, with no coordinated argumentative clauses and one argumentative act (the question), so it is not several jobs in one sentence; T25 - list + dash + question has the shape of a reveal, but the list is real and the question is one the section turns on, not a manufactured payoff; T24 - the question is not answered straight away; T26 - the ‘conscious agreement’ repeat above, inherited and doing a job; T03/T11/T19 - the pivot is set up by the paragraph before and carries the section’s live question rather than just announcing or bridging; T09/T13 - a single sentence, nothing equalised or slotted; no first person (T01, C03); nothing moved (T14); no aphorism, negative reveal, closer or recap (T16, T17, T20, T28, T29). LINTER: ‘B4/E15 list or packed sentence’ - accepted: the list is his own four from his published guide and was already in the paragraph as a list before the question; the join adds no item, no clause and no claim, the sentence has one argumentative act, it is about 24 words and reads cleanly aloud, and the article’s voice uses lists freely, so it is not a real packing problem. ‘D9 follows the source order’ - accepted: it is a punctuation join of two sentences kept in their own order, nothing reordered or moved, and T13 and T09 were checked above. I read the writer’s ADMISSION.json after my own pass; its reasons agree with mine.
